## Appearance

Marilla is a tall, thin, and angular woman with sallow cheeks. Her dark hair, which is touched with gray, is consistently worn twisted up behind her in a hard little knot. Over the years, she has grown even thinner, with grayer hair and hard, work-worn hands.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised P13](../source/v01-c01.md#nw-v01-c01-p0013), [v1 CHAPTER XIII. The Delights of Anticipation P11](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0011), [v2 XII A Jonah Day P39](../source/v02-c12.md#nw-v02-c12-p0039), [v3 ch.Gables P2](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0002)_

## Personality

A woman of narrow experience, rigid conscience, and sensible disposition, this character is practical, non-imaginative, and strongly values neatness and order. Stoic, self-contained, and repressed, she considers displays of deep emotion to be unseemly and is prone to being sarcastic, particularly after headaches or any self-betrayal. She is strict, stern, and inexorable when enforcing discipline, often feeling driven to drill a tranquil uniformity of disposition into others and clinging firmly to her duties. Unsympathetic in speech, she detests cats, refrains from criticizing ministers as a matter of principle, and is fond of tacking morals onto her remarks. Over time, her disposition has noticeably mellowed. Beyond her domestic demeanor, she is skilled at crafting braided mats and is celebrated locally for making currant wine.

## History

Marilla Cuthbert raised [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) after adopting her fourteen years earlier, despite having lived there for sixty years and never traveling more than sixty miles from home. Having been raised under traditional childhood discipline and kept still when told as a child, Marilla initially reacted with shock when [Matthew](../character/matthew-cuthbert.md) brought home a girl instead of a boy. Though she intended to return [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), Marilla felt pity upon learning of the child's past hardships and resolved to raise and educate her properly. Over time, she developed a deep affection for [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), comforting her through various mishaps, encouraging her education, and proudly supporting her success on the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination. Following Matthew's sudden death and receiving news from an oculist that she faced potential blindness, Marilla was spared selling [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) chose to forego college to stay and teach locally. Later, Marilla took in her orphaned twin cousins, [Davy](../character/davy-keith.md) and [Dora](../character/dora.md) Keith, enduring a hectic first six months with Davy's unruly behavior before deciding to keep them permanently. To enable [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to attend [Redmond College](../codex/places.md#redmond-college) without worrying about the household, Marilla invited the newly widowed [Rachel Lynde](../character/rachel-lynde.md) to move into [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables). Marilla eventually celebrated Anne's marriage to [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md), and she traveled to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds) to attend their first [Christmas](../codex/places.md#merry-christmas) dinner and support [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) through the heartbreaking loss of her first baby.

## Quotes

> “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER VI. Marilla Makes Up Her Mind P35](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0035)

> "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"
>
> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P2](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0002)

> "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."

> — Marilla Cuthbert — [v1 CHAPTER X. Anne’s Apology P4](../source/v01-c10.md#nw-v01-c10-p0004)

> "and I can’t prevent her, for her father aids and abets her. She’s always poring over a book. I’m glad she has the prospect of a playmate—perhaps it will take her more out-of-doors."
>

> “I’ll go and have another look,” said Marilla, determining to be just. “If you put that brooch back it’s there still. If it isn’t I’ll know you didn’t, that’s all!”

## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--marilla-cuthbert.md)

Marilla became Anne's adoptive mother and dear friend after initially expecting to adopt a boy to help on the farm. Though shocked by the mix-up and initially inclined to return her, Marilla decided to keep [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) after seeing the harsh alternative of her becoming a servant to Mrs. [Blewett](../character/blewett.md). Their relationship grew through Marilla's efforts to educate [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) in religion, manners, and discipline, eventually evolving into deep mutual affection as they shared both domestic life and profound grief.
